bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's saved run feeds the staged 29-byte witness to Samba's `fuzz_ndr_nbt_TYPE_STRUCT`. The first four bytes are the generic NDR fuzz header `00 00 0a 00`, so the harness keeps `TYPE_STRUCT`, selects NBT public struct 10 (`nbt_netlogon_packet`), and passes the remaining 25 bytes as stub data into `ndr_pull_nbt_netlogon_packet`. That parser reads command `0x0012` (`LOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST`) and dispatches into `NETLOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST`. Because `nbt_netlogon_packet` is `[flag(NDR_NOALIGN)]`, the request parser's initial `ndr_pull_align(ndr, 4)` is a no-op: bytes `20 20` become `request_count = 0x2020`, `00 00`, `00 00`, and `00` decode the empty `computer_name`, `user_name`, and `mailslot_name`, `acct_control = 0x20202020`, and the following `00 00 00 00` decode `sid_size = 0`. The exact vulnerable build allocates `uint8_t st[f->struct_size]` without zeroing it first, and the `sid_size == 0` path zeros only `r->sid`; it never assigns `r->_pad`, so `_pad.data` and `_pad.length` keep stale stack contents. The final print walk re-enters the same request arm and unconditionally executes `ndr_print_DATA_BLOB(ndr, "_pad", r->_pad)`, which reaches `dump_data_cb`. In the reproduced ASAN run, the stale pointer passed as `_pad.data` was `0x60b000000150`, 96 bytes into a 104-byte talloc region that sanitizer reports as freed by `TALLOC_FREE(mem_ctx)`, so `dump_data_cb`'s first byte-format read triggers the reported heap-use-after-free.

source.description: First non-harness parser step on the vulnerable path. After the fuzz header has selected `nbt_netlogon_packet`, this statement consumes the first stub field and materializes the union switch value used by both pull-time and print-time dispatch.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is 29 bytes with sha256 `b06e89e66152b6f52339ef773a58cbb92f0be464251d8c849611d7669cb3b9c2` and begins `00 00 0a 00 12 00 20 20 ...`. The 4-byte fuzz header `00 00 0a 00` keeps `TYPE_STRUCT` and selects NBT public struct 10 (`nbt_netlogon_packet`); `ndr_pull_netlogon_command()` then reads the first stub field `0x0012` as `LOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled control value that suppresses `_pad` initialization is created here. Under the enclosing `nbt_netlogon_packet` `NDR_NOALIGN` semantics, `ndr_pull_align(ndr, 4)` at line 261 does not skip any bytes, so `20 20` become `request_count = 0x2020`, `00 00`, `00 00`, and `00` yield the three empty names, `20 20 20 20` become `acct_control = 0x20202020`, and the following `00 00 00 00` decode `sid_size = 0`.

root_cause.description: The selected public-struct backing store is created on the stack without initialization, so any fields the later NDR pull path does not overwrite retain stale stack contents.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by inserting `memset(st, '\0', sizeof(st));` in this file before `f->ndr_pull(ndr_pull, pull_push_print_flags, st);`.

sink.description: Closest project sink to the ASAN crash. `dump_data_cb` formats the `_pad` blob byte-by-byte and dereferences the stale `buf` pointer passed down from `ndr_print_DATA_BLOB`.
sink.note: The saved ASAN run reports `READ of size 1` here at address `0x60b000000150`.

parser_admitted.description: After the generic 4-byte fuzz header is accepted and public struct 10 is selected, the harness enters the `nbt_netlogon_packet` parser on the remaining 25 stub bytes.
parser_admitted.condition: The witness header has flags `0x0000` and struct selector `0x000a`, so `find_struct(&FUZZ_PIPE_TABLE, function, &f_buffer)` returns `nbt_netlogon_packet` and the harness calls `f->ndr_pull(...)` instead of returning early.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness accepts the generic 4-byte NDR fuzz header, selects NBT public struct 10, and parses the remaining 25 bytes into an uninitialized scratch buffer `st`.
The outer NBT parser materializes `command = LOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST` and dispatches the union into the `NETLOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST` arm.

Under the outer packet's `NDR_NOALIGN` semantics, the checked-in request parser decodes `sid_size = 0`; on that path it zeroes `sid` but never assigns `_pad`, so `_pad.data` and `_pad.length` remain the stale bytes already present in non-zeroed `st`.
The final print walk re-enters the same request arm and unconditionally passes the stale `_pad` blob to `ndr_print_DATA_BLOB`.
`dump_data_cb` dereferences the stale blob pointer byte-by-byte, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: Root cause. The scratch object backing the selected public struct starts as raw stack bytes. Any optional field that later takes a 'not present' branch will keep whatever stale pointer/length pair was already in that slot until something explicitly overwrites it.

Source. After the witness header `00 00 0a 00` selects public struct 10 `nbt_netlogon_packet`, the parser consumes the first stub field as the union switch. The stub begins `12 00`, so this materializes `command = LOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST (18)` in the same `st` buffer that was left uninitialized in step 1.
Because step 2 set `command` to 18, the union pull enters the `NETLOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST` arm and starts filling that member inside the same `st` buffer.

Within that request arm, the enclosing `NDR_NOALIGN` packet semantics make line 261's `ndr_pull_align(ndr, 4)` a no-op, so the stub bytes are consumed as `request_count = 0x2020`, empty `computer_name`, empty `user_name`, empty ASCII `mailslot_name`, `acct_control = 0x20202020`, and then `sid_size = 0`. This materializes the control value that suppresses the optional SID/pad subcontext.

The `sid_size == 0` branch skips `ndr_pull_DATA_BLOB` entirely and only zeroes `r->sid`. No code on this path assigns `r->_pad.data` or `r->_pad.length`, so those fields remain the stale stack contents left in `st` by step 1.

ASAN's free stack identifies this statement as the free site of the stale pointee later read through `_pad.data`. The saved static artifacts do not show which earlier stack residue copied that freed address into `st`; they only establish the observed lifetime fact that the eventual pointee had already been invalidated.

During the final print walk on the same request arm, the generated printer unconditionally treats `_pad` as a live blob. The saved crash PC falls inside this call instruction, showing that the stale `_pad` pair from step 5 is what gets handed to the blob-dump helper.

ASAN sink. `ndr_print_DATA_BLOB` reaches `ndr_dump_data`, which passes `_pad.data` and `_pad.length` as `buf,len` into this loop. In the reproduced run the first dereference of `buf[i]` hit `0x60b000000150`, inside a 104-byte talloc region that sanitizer marks freed, and triggered the reported `heap-use-after-free READ of size 1`.

allocation_context.note: ASAN says the stale pointer later read at step 8 points 96 bytes into the 104-byte talloc root created by `mem_ctx = talloc_init("ndrfuzz");` here.

free_context.note: ASAN's free stack reports the same talloc root as freed by `TALLOC_FREE(mem_ctx);`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json, plus the checked-in vulnerable sources under `_work/src/samba`; the non-persisted generated `bin/default/librpc/gen_ndr/ndr_nbt.c` callsites come from the saved ASAN line map.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partially. ASAN's pointee is a talloc root allocated at line 235 and freed at line 317, while the traced root cause is the non-zeroed stack buffer at line 242 that leaves `_pad.data` and `_pad.length` stale when `sid_size == 0`. The static artifacts close how a stale heap address can survive into `_pad`, but they do not identify the exact earlier stack residue that produced `0x60b000000150`.

evidence_note: The checked-in vulnerable sources `lib/fuzzing/fuzz_ndr_X.c` and `librpc/ndr/ndr_nbt.c` / `librpc/idl/nbt.idl` are preserved under `_work/src/samba`. The runtime-generated `bin/default/librpc/gen_ndr/ndr_nbt.c` file is not preserved under this result bundle, so the outer-parser and printer callsites are grounded by the saved ASAN stack line map and the matching checked-in request-parser / IDL layout rather than by reopening the emitted file itself.
patch_resolves_note: Yes, at source level. The staged patch inserts `memset(st, '\0', sizeof(st));` into `lib/fuzzing/fuzz_ndr_X.c` before `f->ndr_pull(...)`, so step 5 can no longer reuse stale `_pad` contents when `sid_size == 0`. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so this is patch-grounded reasoning rather than differential runtime proof.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 saved `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_19463 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which executed `/out/fuzz_ndr_nbt_TYPE_STRUCT /tmp/poc` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 1` with stack `dump_data_cb -> ndr_dump_data -> ndr_print_NETLOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST`.

format.name: Samba NDR TYPE_STRUCT fuzz input
format.contract: Exactly the staged 29-byte blob `gt_results/arvo_19463/poc` with sha256 `b06e89e66152b6f52339ef773a58cbb92f0be464251d8c849611d7669cb3b9c2`. Bytes 0..1 are fuzz flags `0x0000`, so the target stays on `TYPE_STRUCT`; bytes 2..3 are struct selector `0x000a`, which selects public struct 10 `nbt_netlogon_packet`; bytes 4..28 are the NDR stub. Because `nbt_netlogon_packet` carries `NDR_NOALIGN`, the request parser's `ndr_pull_align(ndr, 4)` does not skip any bytes: the stub encodes `command = LOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST`, `request_count = 0x2020` from bytes `20 20`, empty `computer_name` from `00 00`, empty `user_name` from `00 00`, empty ASCII `mailslot_name` from `00`, `acct_control = 0x20202020`, `sid_size = 0`, `nt_version = 0x20202020`, and both tokens `0x2020`. Those exact semantics keep the request arm live while making the vulnerable build skip `_pad` initialization and later print the stale `_pad` blob.
